 Print Bigg Boss 20 contestant Manish Goel's wife Poonam Narula Goel has finally addressed the ongoing discussion around her husband's reaction to Qazi Touqeer's constant provocation and remarks. She has come out strongly in his support and has called out Qazi's repeated remarks, alleging that Manish has been subjected to constant poking, age-shaming and condescending comments. Explaining why the word 'Professor' triggers Manish, Poonam revealed that what initially started as a prank gradually crossed a line, "I have been patient and stayed silent for over a month, but it's high time I put this out. I'll speak in detail after tomorrow's episode, but for now, I want people to understand why Manish reacts to the word "Professor. Ever since Manish entered the house, Qazi has constantly poked him with names like "Gyani Baba" and "Professor. " It initially started as a prank played by Qazi where other housemates also joined in. Manish had no idea about it but he still took it sportingly, joined them and even danced along (which wasn't telecasted). However, Qazi kept taking it further with condescending remarks and age-shaming. When Manish finally asked him to stop and draw a line, Qazi told the camera that he would make Manish cry and wouldn't stop. That is the real reason behind Manish's reaction on the word "Professor." Poonam further clarified that Manish has never deliberately approached Qazi to create confrontations or gain screen time. She believes his reactions are a reflection of his personality rather than a strategy to stay relevant, "My husband never approaches Qazi to pick a fight. He doesn't care about screen time. If he did, he would have done things purely for footage, but he doesn't. He is emotional, sometimes dramatic, and speaks in strong words. He is North Indian man born in the 70s. That is his personality. Just because the younger generation may not relate to his way of speaking or reacting doesn't mean he is pretending. He is a genuinely nice family man, but he will react when someone constantly pokes him, age-shames him or makes inappropriate poop jokes around him. That is simply not his class. You may love Qazi, but don't be so blinded by that support that you ignore the other side. If Manish cared about elimination, he wouldn't have sacrificed his lifeline for Qazi." Watch From Riya Ahir, Mahhi Vij to Qazi Touqeer, here’s the contestant lineup for Bigg Boss 20 Poonam also questioned why viewers expect Manish to behave like someone he is not, emphasising that his age, personality and individuality should not become reasons for ridicule. Concluding her statement, Poonam said: "In 2026, if people cannot accept a simple, genuinely nice 51-year-old man without expecting him to jump around, abuse others or play along with every kind of stupidity, then that's disappointing and immature.  Manish speaks this way in real life. He loves and takes pride in his language, Shudh Hindi. He is an actor, and we are proud of him. But sometimes, you need to look beyond edited footage and look into a person's eyes to understand when they are genuinely hurt and when they are acting. It's disappointing to see what people choose to endorse today. But we will always stand by each other as a family. Poonam Narula Goel Lots of love, Mannu. Mahadev is watching over you." Poonam's statement brings the focus back to the context behind Manish's behaviour and makes her position clear: she believes his reactions should not be dismissed as drama when, according to her, they stem from repeated provocation.
